canonical.title: Throwing away Windows: a replacement plan for an actual installed-software inventory

children.title: Your .NET + SQL Server stack on Linux: what actually replaces what
children.summary: Rider replaces Visual Studio + ReSharper on Linux at the cost of the WinForms/WPF designers; SQL Server itself moves cleanly to a container, but SSMS has no Linux successor now that Azure Data Studio is dead.

children.title: Microsoft 365 on Linux in 2026: what you actually lose
children.summary: Office, Teams and mail are a tolerable compromise on Linux in 2026; OneDrive sync and OneNote are the two places where the gap is real.

children.title: The utility belt: per-tool Linux verdicts for a Windows power user (2026)
children.summary: Per-tool verdicts for the Windows-only utilities in an actual installed-software inventory: most transfer cleanly, AutoHotkey and Power Automate Desktop have no single answer, and Wayland is the variable that decides the rest.

children.title: Multi-monitor, window management and the desktop shell: replacing DisplayFusion, Fences, FancyZones and X-Rite on Linux
children.summary: KDE Plasma 6.7 is the only Linux desktop that replaces most of DisplayFusion and FancyZones natively; Fences has no real equivalent and the X-Rite workflow becomes ArgyllCMS/DisplayCAL plus a per-screen ICC profile.

children.title: Gaming after the switch: your library survives, the NVIDIA App does not
children.summary: Both installed games run under Proton — Planetfall is Gold/Deck-Playable and Fall Guys' EAC is Linux-enabled — so the only hard loss is the NVIDIA App and Game Bar tooling layer.

children.title: Legion hardware, peripherals and the two corporate VPNs on Linux
children.summary: Neither corporate VPN blocks the switch — Harmony SASE ships an official Linux agent and WatchGuard is reachable with plain OpenVPN; the real losses are QuantumENGINE, Dolby, XTU and Lenovo's AI/Space bloat.

children.title: Escape hatches for the leftovers: Wine, a VM, passthrough, or just keep the partition
children.summary: Wine for single-window utilities, a local Windows VM for Visual Studio and SSMS, RDP for the corporate cluster — and no GPU passthrough on a muxless Legion.
